chunks: Ahmad ibn Ali al-Razi, from Abu Dharr Ahmad ibn Abi Surah (who is Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Abdullah al-Tamimi and was a Zaidi), said: I heard this story from a group who narrate it from my father (may Allah have mercy on him).

That he went to al-Hayr. He said: When I arrived at al-Hayr, I saw a handsome young man praying. Then he bid me farewell and I bid him farewell, and we left. We arrived at al-Mashra. He said to me: O Abu Surah, where are you headed? I said: To Kufa. He said to me: With whom? I said: With the people. He said to me: No, you will go with us. I said: Who is 'us'? He said: We do not mean anyone else but me. He said: So we walked through the night until we were at the graveyard of Masjid al-Sahla. He said to me: That is your place; if you wish, proceed. Then he said to me: You will pass by Ibn al-Zarari, Ali ibn Yahya, and say to him: He will give you the money that is with him. I said to him: Why would he give it to me? He said to me: Say to him: With the sign that it is such and such dinars and such and such dirhams, and it is in such and such a place, and covered with such and such a cover. I said to him: And who are you? He said: I am Muhammad ibn al-Hasan. I said: What if he does not accept from me and asks for proof? He said: I am behind you. He said: So I came to Ibn al-Zarari and said to him: He gave it to me. I said to him: The signs that he told me, and I told him: He had said to me: I am behind you. He said: There is nothing after this [needed], and said: Only Allah Almighty knew of this, and he gave me the money.

key_terms.أَنَا وَرَاءَكَ: I am behind you (a phrase indicating support or presence)
key_terms.ابْنُ الزَّرَّارِيِّ: Ibn al-Zarari, a companion of the Imams
key_terms.مَسْجِدُ السَّهْلَةِ: Masjid al-Sahla, a famous mosque in Kufa

ai.seo_question: What signs did the Imam Muhammad ibn al-Hasan give to Ahmad ibn Abi Surah to verify his identity?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* illustrates the concept of *al--Nujum* (stars) or prominent companions who maintained contact with the Imam during the Minor Occultation (*al-Ghayb al-Sughra*). The specific, verifiable details regarding the hidden wealth of Ali ibn Yahya al-Zarari serve as a rational proof (*hujjah*) of the Imam’s divine knowledge (*ilm al-ghaybah*), reinforcing the legitimacy of his authority despite his physical absence from public view.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 234 - It is narrated from Ahmad bin Ali Raazi from Abu Zar Ahmad bin Abi Surah, same is reported by Muhammad bin Hasan bin Abdullah Tamimi and he was a Zaidiyyah; that he said:

“Once I went to Heer and saw a handsome youth praying there. After that the two of us reached Mashra. He asked: O Abu Surah, where are you headed?” I said: To Kufa. He asked: But with whom? I said: With other people. He said: No, you will travel with us. I asked: What do you mean: ‘with us’? He replied: With me. Thus the two of us set out from there and when we reached the graveyard of Masjid Sahla, he said: That place is near your destination, if you want, you may proceed. He also said: You should go to Ibn Raazi Ali bin Yahya, who will give to you some money, which is with him. I asked: Why would he give me anything? He replied: You mention the amount, where it is placed and with what it is covered. So I asked: Who are you? He replied: I am Muhammad bin Hasan Askari. I asked: What if he refuses to give me anything in spite of the signs? He said: I am behind you. Ibn Abi Surah says: When I went to Ibn Raazi and mentioned the signs, he gave that amount to me. I told him that he had said that he was behind me. Ibn Raazi said: After this sign there is no need of any verification as other than the Almighty Allah, no one had any knowledge of it.
